marta: Quick check — streaming + AbortController/context cancellation across SDKs. We have an internal app that aborts mid-stream and in Node the socket FDs stick around; in Python the task cancels cleanly. Anyone seen divergent cleanup patterns?

kevin: Repro I put together. Node 18 fetch + AbortController: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal });
res.body.on('data', d => { /* keep reading */ });
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 2000);
```
When abort fires the request rejects but the underlying socket sometimes stays open (on Linux you see FD count not drop). Our wrapper currently only rejects the promise but doesn't call `res.body.destroy()` in the abort handler.

josh: For Go we rely on context cancellation: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)` then `req = req.WithContext(ctx)`. If we cancel, net/http handles it and the server sees cancel. But we had a bug where retries didn't `resp.Body.Close()` on the error path — that leaked connections. Worth adding a test for retry flow.

ella: Python notes: we use `httpx.AsyncClient.stream()` in the async SDK. Typical pattern: `async with client.stream('GET', url) as r:`. If the task is cancelled (asyncio.CancelledError) httpx closes the connection but only if the exception propagates out of the `with` block. If someone swallows CancelledError, it can hang. Also be mindful of `asyncio.shield()` use.

kevin: TL;DR: three separate fixes: (1) Node wrapper should explicitly destroy body on abort, (2) Go retry paths must always close body even if we plan to retry, (3) Python docs + example for correct cancel handling. I can open a Node PR for the destroy behavior.

marta: Nice. Can you also capture a tiny repro that counts FDs before/after? That makes it easier to validate in CI.

kevin: Will do. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1234 (draft) — includes unit + small FD-count script. Posting the gist in the PR. cc @josh for Go followups.

josh: I'll add a retry-path test in `eng-runtime` repo and link it here. Also will grep for missing `defer resp.Body.Close()` patterns.

ella: For Python I can add a snippet to the SDK docs showing proper `try/except` around streaming so people don't accidentally swallow CancelledError. Example: 
```py
try:
    async with client.stream('GET', url) as r:
        async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes():
            process(chunk)
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    # ensure the task is cancelled and connection closed
    raise
```

kevin: One extra gotcha I hit: if we wrap fetch in our own EventEmitter-style stream, make sure the abort handler is attached before initiating request; otherwise a fast server can finish and we never wire cleanup.

devex-bot: Reminder: when the PR merges add a changelog line under `fixes` and tag `eng-runtime` and `eng-sdk`.

marta: Thanks all — assigning Node fix to kevin, Go retry test to josh, Python docs to ella. I'll add tasks to the sprint and ping eng-runtime for review. :thumbsup:
